events.body: The road drowns under iron-red water where hand-long leeches turn at your shadow, flashing pale bellies. Dry ground waits twenty strides on. A hot blade might hold them back; speed might deny them any grip.

outcomes.success: You heat steel until old oil smokes, then sweep the hot blade just under the surface. Leeches recoil hissing. You reach the far bank unfed.
outcomes.failure: The blade cools before the channel clears. Parasites fasten beneath your clothes short of dry ground, bleeding on after you tear them free. Your footprints carry blood.

outcomes.success: You enter at a run and never let a boot settle. Dark shapes strike and miss behind every stride. The far bank takes you breathless and untouched.
outcomes.failure: A drowned curb catches your toe and throws you chest-deep. Leeches find skin before you stand. You rip them away with muddy fingers and carry infected bites onward.

outcomes.victory: You go in swinging and crush the swarm into the mud until the water runs clear. A drowned kit bag gives up wrapped bandages and marsh poultice herbs.

events.body:
The boat is narrow enough for one passenger and moored to a road sign standing waist-high out of black water. The ferryman's coat is sewn over with ticket stubs, hundreds of them, layered like scales and gone soft at the edges.

They do not want your bottles and they do not want parts. What they want is one true account of the road behind you, told properly, and they say so while coiling the pole rope as though the price were an ordinary one.

Downstream of the mooring the current wrinkles in a long straight line. Something under there runs level: a service road, curbs still holding their edges, buried under a foot or two of flood. It would carry a person across without a boat, if the person read it correctly and the water had not taken a section out of the middle.

The ferryman watches you look at the channel instead of at them.

outcomes.success:
You give them the part of the journey that makes you least impressive: the door you did not open and the name you never thought to ask for.

Unnecessary detail is how a ferryman tests an account, and yours carries too much of it to have been assembled on the bank. They pole across without another question, and you sit the whole way over, the only stretch of this day you have not walked. On the far side they press a stoppered bottle into your hand, bitter tonic brewed thick for travelers who have swallowed this water, and push off before you can work out what you owe them.
outcomes.failure:
You reach for meaning before you have earned any attention: a shape to the road, a lesson at the end of it, the kind of telling that improves every time it is told. The ferryman lets you get four sentences in.

Then the pole goes down and the boat is leaving, and you are wading. Cold current works in under the pack straps, and something below the surface opens a line across your shin that you do not find until the far bank. The crossing takes a long hour, and it finishes your account for nobody.

outcomes.success:
The wrinkle holds straight for sixty strides, and the reeds standing over the buried road lean differently from the reeds beside it. You walk the curb line with water at your waist and both arms out, testing every step before it takes weight.

Halfway across, your boot finds a junction box wedged against the curb. It comes up trailing weed, and the fittings inside it are dry enough to be worth carrying. When you climb out on the far side and look back, the boat is gone and the sign stands alone in the channel.
outcomes.failure:
The curb runs true until it does not. Where floodwater tore the road out, the shelf ends in open depth, and the current has you sideways before your foot finds anything to argue with.

You swim four bad strokes, catch reed roots, and haul out on a bank you did not choose. The pack comes up with you. Whatever was riding loose in the belt loops goes on downstream, and you stand in the shallows watching the surface for anything of yours that floats, until watching stops being worth the daylight.

events.body: Three skiffs slide from the reeds with their engines wrapped in cloth. The riders carry short guns high above the water and steer by poles rather than noise. One gestures for your pack while another cuts off the raised path behind you. A chemical rainbow spreads between the boats. The raiders avoid touching it, though whether from knowledge or performance is impossible to tell before they close.

outcomes.victory: Your first shots punch through the nearest skiff’s waterline. Its crew overturns while the others choose distance over rescue. Two dry shells, a sealed bottle, and a girder cleaver wired to the gunwale float inside a tied case, salvage from an ambush that leaves widening rings among the reeds.

outcomes.success: You name symptoms produced by the rainbow and point to stains on their own poles. The lead raider hesitates long enough for doubt to spread between boats. You enter thick reeds before anyone volunteers to test the water.
outcomes.failure: They have poled this stain for weeks and know precisely what it does and does not do. Nobody punishes the bluff. The lead rider holds his skiff against the path, opens your pack himself, and lifts out whatever tablets and bandages it is carrying. Then he hands it back, and every gun stays politely raised until you are past the last boat.

outcomes.outcome: The smoke bomb blooms low over the water and turns boats, reeds, and path into the same gray absence. You move by touch until engines cough behind you. When air clears, one useful escape has become an empty casing.

events.body: A rural clinic rides floodwater on timber stilts, lower rooms dark with algae. The supports climb toward an intact pharmacy window. Inside, cabinets gape at water level under branching mold. Below is steadier — and closer to spores.

outcomes.success: You spread weight across three supports and slip through the pharmacy window. A medkit and painkillers hide behind a childproof latch that beat hurried looters.
outcomes.failure: A wet crossbeam parts from its nails and drops you hard. You catch the frame short of the flood, ankle folded. The pharmacy stays above.

outcomes.success: You pole-test each lower doorway and follow the room where air still moves outward. Sealed bandages and bitter tonic wait above its mold line.
outcomes.failure: The floor holds, but your first cabinet breathes out a trapped cloud. Fever starts warm behind the eyes before daylight. The clinic shrinks through mist behind you.

outcomes.outcome: You read the water-stained dosage chart and measure the right dose from dusty vials. Fever breaks while you rest, and old infections fade with it.

events.body: Root and rusted cable hold an old footbridge together over fast black water. The deck shifts before you step on, with no wind in the reeds. Rope could steady it section by section. Something pale surfaces between the pylons.

outcomes.success: You cross in short steps timed between the bridge’s long swings. The far boards lift under your last stride as vines tear free behind. Nobody should repeat the method.
outcomes.failure: A cable parts like a struck instrument and hurls you into the rail. You cling as the deck tilts, then crawl on. Bruised ribs record every demand the bridge made.

outcomes.success: You thread line through vine and cable, tightening each section before trusting weight. On the far side you cut the anchor free. The crossing stands for whoever comes next.
outcomes.failure: The knots hold exactly as tied. Tying them across a moving deck costs more than the crossing, and your hands finish cramped shut. The line holds one side.

outcomes.victory: You stay clear of the throat and open the floater's gut in knee-deep water. The gland vial and sealed bottle are yours. Your hands stop shaking and hold steady.

events.body:
Pale lights repeat beneath the drowned road: three close together, one apart, then nothing. Each cycle begins farther east, running alongside the roadbed before it curves away into deeper reeds. The rhythm is too even for anything feeding and too mobile for a lamp on a pole.

Between you and the sequence lies a bank of black stems solid enough to walk. You watch it long enough to be certain. The reeds on either side of it lean downstream; the bank leans against them. It is traveling. On its near edge, above the waterline, sits one boot with its laces still tied.

Two words have been cut into the marker post at your knee, deep enough to have outlasted a season of rain. Reed widow.

Exposed roots run the long way around, ankle deep and slow. The drainage cut the lights gather in is the short way, and nothing has crossed it while that bank has been sitting on it.

outcomes.success:
You go in on the dark part of the cycle and stand still when the lights return, three and one, and you do that eleven times before your knee finds a lid under the silt.

It is a civil-defense drum, and the seal is the only reason anything inside is still worth carrying out. Two bottles and a purifier ampoule come up in your hands. The sequence is already resuming farther east, keeping its measure, marking a route for nobody at all.

You reach the far bank with grit under your nails and both boots on your feet.
outcomes.failure:
You hold the count for thirty strides. Then the count begins holding you: the gap between the three and the one narrows, widens, narrows again, and the line you are walking bends off the roadbed while you are still pleased with yourself for keeping to it.

The silt you go into is loose and warm and lets up slow bubbles wherever your weight lands. There is a taste at the back of your teeth like a coin held too long in the mouth. You wade out along your own churn, and after that you have to stop every few hundred strides with your hands on your knees.

outcomes.success:
You take the roots. Every one of them has to be trodden before it is trusted, and going the long way around costs you the whole gray middle of the day.

The lights keep pace below you for the entire distance, three and one, three and one, holding the same twenty strides off your shoulder. Where the roots finally lift onto hard ground the sequence stops, waits through one dark interval, and starts back the way it came.

You never find out what was under those pulses, or whether anything was.
outcomes.failure:
The visible bank holds for two hundred strides and then closes into reed and tangled root that will not let a person stand upright. You go through it anyway, because turning back means the water.

You carry the pack overhead through the worst of it, double back twice where the root mat gives under you, and come out the far side with your arms shaking and your shirt soaked to the collar. The lights are still working their cycle behind you, unhurried, exactly where they were when you decided not to test them.

outcomes.victory:
It goes still, and the raft it has been wearing comes apart across the cut in loose mats of stem and root.

Underneath is the clutch. Pale eggs lie in a line along its back, three close and one apart, going out one after another as the water reaches them. That was the pattern the whole time.

You wade the cut on your own feet, find a civil-defense drum in the silt at the eastern end, and come up with two bottles, a purifier ampoule, and the widow's hide. The boot stays where it is. Whoever crosses here next will not have to read the water first.

events.body:
Wood smoke comes through the reeds in threads, from a hut standing on poles that do not match: two mill posts, a length of pipe, a telegraph pole with its insulators still on. Bundles of herbs hang under the eaves, dry in air that has not been dry for weeks, which takes a fire kept going every day by somebody who knows how to keep one.

No boat is tied at the ladder. The ladder is down.

You are eleven strides out when a shutter closes on the near side of the hut. Not slammed. Closed, at the speed of a hand that wanted to be sure of you first.

Calling out from here gives whoever is behind that shutter time to decide what you are. Going in quiet decides it for them.

outcomes.success:
The answer comes from behind the hut rather than inside it: a platform in the reeds you had not found, and an herbalist on it with a crossbow lowered across her knees. She trades from there and never invites you closer.

Road news buys supplies. She takes the state of the raised path east and gives you two ration bars and a bottle of tonic for it, then corrects you once, flatly, in the voice of somebody who has watched people get it wrong: the leech water is the channel before the road bends, not the one after.
outcomes.failure:
Your voice goes out across the water and nothing comes back. The chimney keeps smoking. The closed shutter shifts a hand's width against the wind, holds there, and does not open.

You call twice more, because leaving after one call is the same as admitting what you were prepared to do if nobody was home. Then you take the long way around, watched by something you cannot locate, and the reeds click behind you for half a mile afterward, turning every pause into a decision about whether to look back.

outcomes.success:
You go through the shallows on the blind side and come up under the floor. The hut is empty. The smoke is a banked fire of green reed and dung, built to burn slow and unattended, which is the trick that keeps the herbs dry and the insects off the doorway.

A filter mask hangs on a nail by the hearth with a note beneath it: whoever secures the door may have this. You secure the door. You also take one ration bar out of the tin by the ladder, which the note says nothing about at all.
outcomes.failure:
The dart is in your shoulder before your hand reaches the first pole. It is thin, fletched with reed, and the dose in it is meant to put a person down rather than finish one; heat spreads out from the puncture and your thoughts start arriving late.

You back off through water that has become hard to judge. From the platform behind the hut somebody fits a second dart and then does not use it, and you understand that this was the whole message and you have already received it.

events.body:
The filter station stands on a concrete apron above the flood, and it is still running. Pipes vibrate under the walkway with the sound of water being made to go somewhere it would not go on its own.

Two gauges are mounted beside the door. One still carries pressure east: the needle sits low and holds, which means somebody at the far end of that line is drinking. The other has been unbolted down to bare threads, and the pump beneath it sits dead in its cradle with the housing already open, gears and wound wire inside, a sealed mask in the service cabinet next to it.

The intake screen is choked with reed. Clearing it and resetting the stages would put water back into a pipe whose far end you will never see. The parts are here, in reach, tonight.

outcomes.success:
You clear the screen by hand and then work backward through the stages, resetting each one in turn instead of forcing the final pump to carry the whole line.

Brown becomes cloudy. Cloudy becomes clear, with the flat mineral taste of water that has been pushed through sand. Three bottles fill from the test outlet while the eastern needle climbs and settles, and the pipe under the walkway takes up its work again, carrying pressure toward people who will never know the line was off.
outcomes.failure:
The coupling on the second stage has been corroding under its lagging for years, and renewed pressure finds it inside a minute. It parts at chest height and puts the untreated draw across your face and shirt.

You get the intake shut before the walkway floods. Then you stand in the marsh rinsing with water no cleaner than what you are rinsing off, tasting metal at the back of your teeth, the line closed at both ends now and nothing coming out of it for anybody east of here.

outcomes.success:
The dead housing lifts off its brace without touching the live line beside it. You take the gears, the wound wire, and the mask from the cabinet, and you leave the bolts in a row on the walkway out of a tidiness you cannot account for.

What remains is an empty mount and a stub of pipe. Anyone who climbs up here after you will see at once that the station is no longer a repair somebody might attempt; it is a machine that has been taken apart, and they will not waste a day on it.
outcomes.failure:
The casing shifts off its brace while your hand is behind it and puts your knuckles against the walkway grating with the whole weight of the pump behind them.

You lever it up and get free, and it goes over the edge anyway, into four feet of black water with your blood on it. The mount is empty, the pump is somewhere under the flood, and the station is no easier to restore than it was when you came up the ladder.

events.body:
A body in a yellow raincoat is held against a road marker by its own hood. The coat is clean, which puts her here after the last rain rather than before it.

A waterproof pocket is fastened under the collar, on the side the swelling has not reached yet.

The marker has a length of reinforcing bar driven through it at an angle, ground to a point at the water end by somebody who wanted a spear and a mooring out of the same piece of steel. Under the hem of the coat, plates cut from truck tire show where they are wired onto a vest she is still wearing.

The current works her against the post and lets her back again. Nothing here is in a hurry. Whatever you decide, you will be deciding it in front of her.

outcomes.success:
You turn her by the coat and not by the skin. The pocket holds a strip of radiation tablets, a route map drawn over a printed one, and a laminated card: Lysa Dorn, photographed squinting into a sun nobody has seen in years.

You copy her markings into your own margins, three crossings with one of them struck through twice, and you say the name out loud once, because a name said out loud is harder to lose than a card in a pocket. Then you put her face back under and leave the coat where anyone can see it. A sealed poultice shares the pocket, wrapped against the damp.
outcomes.failure:
The coat tears along a seam where trapped gas has swollen the body, and what comes out of it runs over your forearm and into a cut you had forgotten you were carrying.

You get clear and scrub with silt, which is the worst thing available and the only thing available. The pocket stays fastened. She keeps her name, and you walk east with your arm already hot to the touch, having proved only that a body can still be damaged by somebody in a hurry.

outcomes.outcome:
You wedge a branch between her shoulder and the post so the current cannot work her loose and carry her out into open water, where nobody would ever find her at all.

Yellow shows a long way in this country. Anyone coming up this road looking for a woman in a yellow coat will find her exactly where she stopped, and will be able to do the part you are not doing. You go on with no name, no tablets, and nothing to argue with yourself about later.

outcomes.success:
You work the bar out of the marker in slow chest-deep pulls, a boot braced on the post's footing, keeping the coat behind you where your movements cannot reach it. The last of the length comes free with a wet ring you feel through your teeth.

It is heavier than it looks, and the point is filed rather than broken. Somebody made this on purpose, and drove it in here on purpose, and then did not take it with them when they left this place.
outcomes.failure:
There is no angle to brace against in moving water. Your boots come off the footing twice, and the third attempt takes more out of you than the first two together while the steel travels perhaps a finger's width.

You give the post back to the flood and stand in the shallows breathing hard with your arms hanging. Whoever drove that bar through the marker did it from something solid, and whatever they were standing on is not there anymore.

outcomes.success:
The vest is wired rather than stitched: plates cut from truck tire, overlapped along the ribs, threaded together with fence wire by somebody with pliers and time. Getting it off her takes both hands, careful weight against the post, and longer than respect would prefer.

You wash the silt out of it in the channel and stow it across the top of the pack. It is heavy, and it stops what cloth does not, and it belonged to a woman who was wearing it when whatever happened here happened to her.
outcomes.failure:
Flood silt has packed the wiring solid where the plates overlap, and the wire has rusted into the rubber it was threaded through. You brace against the marker and pull until your arms will not close properly.

She settles deeper with every attempt, tilting away from the post, and you stop while stopping is still your decision and not the current's. The vest stays where it is. So does she, lower in the water now than you found her.

events.body: Rain falls black, each drop spreading an oily ring on standing water. Frogs and insects cut out together. A fallen road sign offers a low metal roof. A tree line stands farther than the storm’s curtain.

outcomes.success: You angle the sign so black runoff drains behind the verge and weight its corners with asphalt. The roof booms but holds. Only your boots take contamination.
outcomes.failure: Wind takes the sign before the last anchor and drives it across your legs. Black water pools under your roof while you fight free. Shelter becomes a trap.

outcomes.success: You reach dense branches before the rain thickens and pull live leaves over exposed gear. The sprint empties your lungs, but canopy spends the drops instead of skin.
outcomes.failure: Black rain overtakes you among reeds with nothing high enough to hide under. You push on while water hunts every seam, reaching the trees spent and glowing.

events.body: A loading-bay door rises alone, shedding rust. Three security drones descend behind it, lenses already searching, reciting an evacuation order decades late. Their control link pulses from a yard relay. Painted blind spots cross the concrete.

outcomes.success: You kill the relay in the silence between commands. All three drones settle like sleeping birds. Intact cells and a portable scanner come free, still warm.
outcomes.failure: The relay jumps frequency as your probe lands, and the yard answers with a blue pulse. Your skull finds concrete. Sounds arrive a half-second behind their makers.

outcomes.success: You learn the arcs first: three lenses, three sweeps, one shared gap. You cross as wire snaps shut behind your heel. Your hands settle, holding the count.
outcomes.failure: One blind spot ends a pace short. Wire takes your ankle and throws you sideways; you cut free before the reel-in. The ankle argues every step out.

outcomes.victory: You bring the swarm down with a scavenged bar, smashing lenses and rotors against concrete. Three power cells and useful scrap come out of the wreckage.

outcomes.success: You wire the probe into the yard relay and feed the swarm its own orders. Two drones settle like sleeping birds, cells intact. Your thoughts feel arranged and quick.
outcomes.failure: The relay answers with a feedback shriek that climbs the probe into your hands. It bursts behind your eyes and keeps ringing after the yard goes silent.

events.body:
Generator Three turns behind a mesh cage whose corner has been cut open and folded back, so somebody stood exactly here once and made a decision. The flywheel wobbles through every revolution. Half the indicator lamps still glow green; the rest have melted into black beads.

A laminated card is zip-tied to the mesh at eye height, printed in the flat language of people who never expected a stranger to read it: GENERATOR THREE CARRIES EMERGENCY STORES AND JACKET COOLING. ISOLATE ONLY UNDER SUPERVISION. Beneath the last line, in pencil, somebody has recorded that supervision left with everyone else.

The copper bus shakes against its ceramic mounts, thick as a wrist. Balancing the phases would answer the card and open whatever the emergency stores have kept dry. Cutting the bus out would answer your pack instead, and the assembly turning behind the mesh makes no distinction between cloth, fingers, and patience.

outcomes.success:
You take the phases one breaker at a time, shedding load off the failing leg and returning it where the card says it belongs, until the wobble goes out of the flywheel between one revolution and the next.

Somewhere down the corridor an emergency locker lets its catch go with a single clean click, the way it was built to when this plant was still worth protecting. Medicine, a stimulant, and a tin of fasteners have stayed dry inside it. Behind you the machine holds its note, and the overhead pipes begin ticking as heat moves back into them.
outcomes.failure:
A charge the panel calls dead comes back up the bus with your hands still inside the cage. Heat blooms through the gloves before you can let go, and letting go costs you the skin of both palms.

You sit on the concrete afterward with your hands open in front of you, because closing them is not available and will not be for a while. The flywheel keeps its stutter. Every green lamp is exactly as green as it was when you arrived.

outcomes.success:
You wedge the flywheel with a bar until the assembly surrenders its momentum, then unwind the bus in heavy lacquered loops that weigh more with every turn around your forearm. It is good metal and there is a great deal of it.

The lamps go out a row at a time. Darkness travels down the connected corridor faster than you could walk it, and the pipes overhead start to contract, knocking as they give back the last heat this place was still making. Your pack is a different weight at the door than it was at the cage.
outcomes.failure:
The improvised brake slips before your sleeve is clear of the housing. Cloth catches, the assembly takes the arm with it, and your shoulder arrives against the mesh a half beat after the rest of you.

You come loose with the limb still attached, and that is the entire good news. The joint sits wrong in its socket now and reports every reach you make afterward, and reaching is most of what the road asks of anybody. The copper stays where it was, turning.

events.body:
Figures stand along the warehouse roof at measured intervals: one at each stairwell, two behind a sandbagged sign, another watching the rail yard and nothing else. Their gear is repaired rather than scavenged, and no weapon wavers while they look you over.

A woman with white welding marks across her mask asks what news travels east. Behind her a road map is pinned to plywood, marked over in three colors and corrected in a fourth, and a field set sits switched on beside it. The freight cars offer a way around, undercarriages sunk in soot and razor filings.

outcomes.success: You trade names, closures, and one warning you would rather have kept. She tests each detail against the plywood, moves a marker two fingers north, and has a ration handed down from the sandbags. Her crew records your face without pretending that it is friendship, which is the honest version of both.
outcomes.failure: Your account disagrees with a signal report the field set took that morning, and they treat the disagreement as procedure rather than as insult. Two of them go through your pack with disciplined hands and keep whatever medicine it holds against the time you cost them. Then they walk you out the long way, at their pace, and it is a long way.

outcomes.victory: Their weakest guard proves neither weak nor alone, but you remain standing when the warehouse falls quiet. The masked woman calls the outcome earned rather than forgiven and slides rifle cartridges and a spike rifle across the roof before granting passage. A furnace maul leans where their smith worked beside a loop of dredge chain, and you take both.

outcomes.success: You crawl beneath freight cars while rooftop attention remains on the road. Couplings hide each movement, and soot swallows the sound. You emerge beyond the final switch unnoticed, carrying no prize except an unchallenged route.
outcomes.failure: The rail yard extends through collapsed cars and blocked switches farther than the roof suggested. You crawl until elbows bleed and muscles shake, escaping observation only by spending the strength needed for the miles ahead.

events.body: A conveyor wakes as you cross, sealed crates jolting toward a slow crusher. Stencils promise medicine, food, riot stock; age erased most. One reachable crate still reads padding and shells. The emergency panel blinks far side.

outcomes.success: You match the belt and swing the crate off by its straps. Folded padding, two dry shells, and a vent-grille guard ride it down.
outcomes.failure: A loose strap winds a roller and takes your forearm along. You wrench back before bone meets mechanism. The belt keeps skin and strength; the crate rides on.

outcomes.success: You trace the emergency circuit past dead switches to the one honest interlock. The line stops mid-stroke. Reserve crates sit down whole: cans and sealed water under dust.
outcomes.failure: The diagrams describe wiring replaced years ago. Each attempt wakes another belt section, and shutdown eats the hour. You leave tired; the crusher works on.

events.body:
A reinforced office stands above the factory floor on pillars. Its door still reads SHELTER CAPACITY 8, and the frame is scratched in a band at chest height by considerably more than eight.

A chemical lock guards the keypad. Personnel notices curl behind dusty glass, close enough to read, dense with anniversaries a manager might have used. Past them a long cabinet stands against the inner wall, a manifest card screwed to its door. An emergency kit is bracketed above the entrance, out of reach without a ladder. The wall panels are thin, and yellow insulation leaks from the seams.

outcomes.success: The personnel board remembers an anniversary the keypad accepts as authority. Inside, eight chairs face a silent radio, and a medical satchel hangs untouched beside painkillers. You take the supplies without disturbing the names written underneath.
outcomes.failure: Your final guess triggers the chemical lockout. Bitter vapor spills from the keypad and coats your mouth before you clear the landing. The dose leaves radiation clicking through your meter while the sealed room keeps its dead arithmetic.

outcomes.success: You cut along existing corrosion, peel the panel inward, and enter between supports. Emergency cans and sealed water wait beneath a table set for eight. The unopened door preserves whatever promise the shelter once made.
outcomes.failure: The wall opens, but insulation pours over your face and into every fold of clothing. You retreat coughing, eyes streaming, your body already heating toward fever. The office remains visible through the hole and unreachable through the fibers.

outcomes.success: The manifest card records every issue and return in a clerk’s shorthand that gives up on dates partway down the column and switches to plain numbers. You read the last return as the number it plainly is and give it to the cabinet lock. The door swings on a hunting rifle and four rounds still in their sleeve.
outcomes.failure: You read the manifest three ways and the cabinet accepts none of them. After the third refusal something inside drops a bar across the mechanism and stops answering anything at all, which is the procedure working exactly as it was written to work. You spend the last of the light in front of a door that has finished deciding about you.

outcomes.success: You climb the pillar bracing with your boots turned sideways on the ribs and work the bracket loose one-handed, holding the kit against your chest as it comes free. The flare gun drops into your palm with three shells still clipped beside it. The bracket above the door hangs empty for the first time since this floor had a shift on it.
outcomes.failure: The bracket holds; the pillar does not. You slide down its corroded face and spend several minutes on the floor deciding that nothing is broken. The kit stays mounted above the door, catching light you can no longer reach.

events.body: Blue flame crawls a loading dock toward ticking pressure drums. Suppression valves stand overhead in mismatched emergency colors. A spill cabinet waits bolted at the dock’s end. The outer fence offers distance if you run now.

outcomes.success: Foam buries the dock before a seal lets go. You strip furnace plates and fittings off the cooled valve, and the spill cabinet yields its sealed injector.
outcomes.failure: A valve bursts and sprays burning residue across your sleeve. You smother it on the floor, but the burn stays bright and wet under dressing.

outcomes.success: You run the fence line as drums start changing shape. The first rupture lands past the concrete wall. Heat takes its share, but no shrapnel finds you.
outcomes.failure: The nearest drum goes before distance becomes shelter. Its wave plants your shoulder and skull into the fence. You wake to falling ash, one ear silent.

events.body:
Three knocks come out of the sealed tank above the processing floor, then a pause you could set a watch by, then three more. You stand through six cycles before the pause explains itself. It lasts exactly as long as the needle takes to climb back to its mark, and nothing that breathes keeps time off a gauge.

The condensation on the inspection hatch is warm under your palm. Low on the outer plates, where the cooling jacket wraps the tank, rings are scorched through the paint one inside another, the size of something that has rested there for years.

Two of the hatch dogs have been backed off a quarter turn from the inside and stopped there.

Somebody added a line to the shift board in grease pencil, beneath the last real entry, in the flat hand of a person filling in a form: KILNBACK IN NUMBER FOUR JACKET. DO NOT VENT. The feed line still has a drain cock on it, and the tank above it is full.

outcomes.success:
You bleed the line down before you touch a dog, and you back them off in the order that keeps the hatch from swinging.

There is a person in the dry chamber. An engineer, three days past the end of their water, wedged above the sump where the heat could not reach through the wall. They come out on your arm, sit on the grating until their eyes work again, and press a field scanner wrapped in oilcloth into your hands because it is the only thing they still own.

They go west. You watch them reach the yard gate on their own feet before you turn away.
outcomes.failure:
The first dog you back off is the one holding the pressure, and it goes from tight to gone between one quarter turn and the next.

What comes out is not steam. It is hot and it is wet and it carries whatever has been standing in that tank since the plant died, straight across your face and down your chest. You get the hatch shut with your shoulder and your eyes closed.

The knocking stops while you are still kneeling on the grating, and does not start again. Your skin stays hot long after the water on it has dried.

outcomes.success:
You put two fingers on the feed pipe and count against the gauge instead of against yourself. Three knocks, and the needle climbs. Silence, and it falls. That is not a valve and it is not a person. It is something that swells when the tank heats and settles when the pressure bleeds, and it has kept that time long enough to be good at it.

So you bleed the pressure off in the part of the cycle when the thing behind the wall is settling, and fill both bottles at the drain cock without the plates shifting once. You will know that rhythm anywhere you hear it again.
outcomes.failure:
You count it four times and get four answers. The interval is exact until you decide it is exact, and then it slips a half second and you are counting up from nothing again, and the harder you listen the more it sounds like a reply to your own listening.

You leave the tank shut. The knocking comes with you through the adjoining pipes, at the same spacing, ahead of you as often as behind, and by the time you are out on the yard you have stopped trusting your own count of anything.

outcomes.victory:
It will not leave the heat, so the heat is where you fight it, in a cooling jacket too narrow for either of you.

When the plates come apart they come apart all at once, and the mass behind them settles into the gap it held and stops answering the gauge.

Two of them are cut sheet with the fittings still on, and you take them. The hatch lifts easily. The engineer climbs down without help, drinks what you can spare, and walks west. You fill both bottles at the drain cock. The needle rises and falls with nothing moving to it. You have that cycle by heart.

events.body: A banded freight pallet hangs over the only clear path on one corroding cable, wires parting with soft pings. The crane cab watches from a rusted ladder, windows black. Seconds under it, or minutes working its controls.

outcomes.success: You go as the swing unloads the weakest strand, unhurried — hurry parts cable. The strands fail two steps past your shadow. Your hands keep doing exactly as told.
outcomes.failure: The cable unbraids at your midpoint. One pallet corner catches your shoulder and rings your head off concrete. You crawl clear while the yard doubles and tilts.

outcomes.success: The cab answers in reluctant jolts. You set the pallet down square and cut the slack cable. Sealed tools and a ration bar pay for the patience.
outcomes.failure: The lever jams halfway and the brake won’t release. You spend an hour on dead circuits before accepting the load stays up. Only daylight is lost.

events.body:
A row of worker lockers survives along the changing-room wall, each door scratched with a family name instead of an employee number. Some list children underneath. Several carry dates that run down in a column and then stop together on the same day.

One door in the row has no name on it and no scratches either, and it is sealed harder than the rest.

Two things in this room were never anybody’s personal property. A security cabinet is bolted through the wall at the end of the bench, its dial worn bright by one hand repeating one sequence for years. Beside it a carrying rig hangs inside a stripped locker frame, bolted through the metal by somebody who meant to come back for it and priced its theft accordingly.

The named doors are shut. Nothing in here needs them opened.

outcomes.success:
The unmarked door gives on the third try without your touching a name. Inside: insulated gloves folded around a roll of bandage, and a barrier plate with a door grip riveted to it standing against the back panel, the sort of thing a person builds across a slow shift and never explains to anybody.

You take all three and shut the door the way you found it. Every named locker stays closed. For once the useful things and the dead are stored in separate boxes, and you are not asked to choose between them.
outcomes.failure:
The latch has a torn edge folded back inside it, and you find that edge with the pad of your hand rather than with your eyes. The cut runs the length of the palm and opens a little further every time you close your grip on anything.

Blood goes across three names you had been careful not to disturb. You bind the hand, the wrap darkens through anyway, and the unmarked door has not moved a finger width.

outcomes.outcome:
You read every visible name once, in the order the row puts them, and then put your hands in your pockets. Twelve families and a column of dates that agree with one another.

No food comes out of this and no equipment either, only a settled understanding of where necessity is supposed to stop. You are still carrying that understanding when the changing room is behind you, and it makes the next problem stand apart into pieces you can pick up one at a time.

outcomes.success:
The dial is worn brightest at four numbers, and the wear is uneven: one of the four has been turned to twice as often as the others. That is a hand, not a combination, and a hand is the part of a procedure that never gets written down.

The cabinet opens on the third attempt. A baton lies in its foam cutout with the charge indicator still showing one bar, held there by a cell built to sit in a dark cabinet for a decade and be ready anyway.
outcomes.failure:
You work the dial through every sequence the wear suggests, and then through the sequences it does not suggest, until the changing room has gone fully dark around your hands.

On the last wrong entry something inside drops a bar across the mechanism and stops answering. The procedure worked. Whatever the guard was told to protect is still protected. You spent a shift of your own proving it, and you leave the dial exactly where you found it.

outcomes.success:
The bolts go through from the inside, so the rig cannot come off the frame; the frame has to come off the wall. You brace a boot against the bench and take the sheet metal apart around the fasteners, slowly, so that the whole row does not follow it down.

The harness comes away with every pouch intact and its straps still soft. There is room in it for the things you have been leaving at the edge of yards like this one, because you had nowhere to put them.
outcomes.failure:
The frame bends instead of tearing. It folds the shoulder strap into a crease across the seam that carries the load, and a crease there finishes a harness, whatever anybody wants to believe about stitching.

You stop before the row goes over onto the benches, partly because the noise would carry through the whole floor and partly because of whose doors they are. What is left will not be worn by anybody now.

events.body: Red lamps ignite one after another down the assembly corridor. A flat voice announces shift evacuation while blast doors begin sealing in sequence toward you. The wall console can freeze the pattern if its surviving circuits still obey. Otherwise, the closing gaps form a race whose finish keeps narrowing. Each door bears dents at shoulder height and deep scratches near the floor, evidence that earlier workers learned exactly how little time the alarm allowed.

outcomes.success: You isolate the timing circuit before the nearest door completes its descent. Every barrier stops at a different height, leaving one clean passage through. The silent alarm lights continue counting a disaster no longer able to move.
outcomes.failure: The console holds one door and hurries the next. Steel comes down across your pack and drives it flat before you can cut the straps loose, and whatever it held takes that weight instead of your spine. You come out the far side lighter than you went in, breathing hard, with the red lamps still counting behind the closed steel.

outcomes.success: You commit before the first gap reaches knee height. Each slide begins before the previous roll ends, boots striking sparks from concrete. The last door closes on your shadow and leaves the alarm voiceless behind steel.
outcomes.failure: Your shoulder reaches the final opening a fraction too late. The safety strip reverses the door after its full weight lands, leaving the joint twisted and swollen. You stagger through before damaged machinery changes its mind.

events.body: Robed figures kneel in ranks across the fused plain, and the rank nearest you carries the worst scarring: old burns polished with oil until they shine like marks of office. Each pilgrim keeps a blade knapped from the ground itself across their knees. They pass a road blessing down the line in alternating halves, and a child walks the ranks listening for anyone who fumbles a half. Behind you a glass ridge would hide a body, though it has been storing the day's heat since morning. The procession lies between you and every route east.

outcomes.success: You give the blessing back with its forgotten final line, and the child stops walking. The rank in front of you opens. An older pilgrim presses two civil-defense tablets and a fistful of pale moss from the offering cloth into your hands, moss to chew, incense to burn, and counts you among the ones the flash decided to keep.
outcomes.failure: One half of the blessing arrives in the wrong order and the line stops answering. They rise as a single body, name you profane, and the flats of their blades find your ribs and your shoulders before the ranks let you out. Distance ends the pursuit. It does not end what your hands are doing.

outcomes.victory: Ceremonial blades break when their owners discover you will not kneel. The surviving pilgrims scatter across their mirrored horizon. You recover purifier fluid, strange edible moss, and a furnace-folded sword from offerings they abandon, then leave before devotion regroups.

outcomes.success: You flatten beneath the ridge and count breaths while the procession passes above. Their song moves east without faltering. When you rise, shallow knee prints remain warm in the glass and every pilgrim is already a distortion.
outcomes.failure: The ridge magnifies the sun instead of blocking it. You remain hidden while heat drains strength and radiation wakes beneath the surface. By the procession’s final verse, concealment has exacted more than discovery might have.

events.body: Wind lifts glittering slivers off the fused plain into a wall of needles. Your meter wakes with the glitter — the flash is going up with it. Layered cloth might turn the smallest shards. An overturned crawler waits across open ground.

outcomes.success: You bind cuffs, collar, and mask before the needles thicken. Glass whispers on layered cloth, cutting fabric instead of flesh. Every knot holds till the wind empties.
outcomes.failure: The wrap loosens under one arm, then everywhere at once. Glass enters every opening and bright-cuts skin already fighting wind. You come out bleeding, cuffs full of unshakable grit.

outcomes.success: You reach the crawler as the storm takes the horizon. Armor soaks the barrage like heavy rain while you brace on the hull, listening to glass fill your tracks.
outcomes.failure: The shining wall catches you in sight of shelter. You dive the last meters through cutting air, reaching the belly with bloody sleeves and nothing left.

events.body: A blast door juts from fused ground at an angle, its number swallowed by black glass. The keypad still blinks green. Through the slit: stocked shelves in undisturbed dust. A maintenance hatch sits lower, swollen shut. Both seams breathe cold.

outcomes.success: You read the placards’ arrows into a digit sequence. Bolts draw back; cold rolls past. Inside, off a shelf stocked for people who never came: purifier, medkit, two ration bars.
outcomes.failure: The last digit wakes a coolant defense, not the lock. Irradiated vapor pours through the keypad housing at eye level. You retreat coughing past a calm green display.

outcomes.success: You break one hinge and guide the hatch inward before its weight falls. The shaft ends in an equipment room: a hazard wrap and radiation tablets by empty suits.
outcomes.failure: The hinge tears from concrete early and the hatch lands across your foot. Leverage and panic make room. You climb out with an ankle too thick for the boot.

events.body:
A human shadow is burned into the only wall still standing, arms raised, its edges gone soft with years of grit. It is old. The pale dust on your sleeve is not. It is settling now, fine as flour, and it was not on you at the last marker.

Boot prints come up out of the west and stop at the wall. Nothing goes back.

Your meter climbs faster than you are walking, which means whatever lifts it is walking too. Ahead, across the floor of a shallow ravine where reflected heat hides the ground, a shadow crosses the glass at a steady pace with nothing above it to cast it.

Under the silhouette a pilgrim has scratched two words and an arrow east: cinder giant. The way you came in stays in plain sight the whole way, and you can turn back at any point before the ravine.

outcomes.success:
The prints pick up again under a shelf of mirrored stone that had been throwing the glare back at you all along, and there is somebody beneath it.

Alive. Dust-sick, gray to the wrists, too far gone to work out which way the ravine runs, and waiting under that shelf for the thing outside to finish passing. It has not finished. You get them onto their feet and take them out the long way across open glass, the shadow working east behind you both, the burned wall in sight ahead the entire time.

On hard ground they give you their scout leathers and a bottle, and go on east.
outcomes.failure:
You follow the prints down into the ravine, where the reflected heat lies over the ground like standing water and every edge of it doubles.

They turn. They come back up the far side. They arrive at the same wall from the other direction and stop in the same place, and you understand that you have walked the outside of a circle somebody else walked first, through a pocket of ground that has been charging you for every stride of it.

You climb out with your legs gone heavy and a dry ache behind both eyes, no wiser about who they were.

outcomes.outcome:
You do not go down. You take the high line east, keeping the burned wall over your shoulder for as long as it will stay in view, and you let the prints stay unfinished.

The shadow crosses the ravine floor twice more while you are still near enough to watch it. Both times you stop walking until it has gone by, because standing still costs less than being seen to move, and both times nothing whatever appears above it to account for it.

Whoever came out of the west stays a set of prints and a distance you chose not to close.

events.body: A machined object smolders in a dustless fresh crater, four black vanes folded round a pulsing seam. The glass beneath softens with every pulse. Cooling it might save a drone core. Marking it and walking away costs nothing but the salvage.

outcomes.success: Water flashes to steam on the casing, but steady cooling slows the pulse. You open the core safely: dense salvage with an intact scanner nested in blackened vanes.
outcomes.failure: The shell contracts and the seam opens toward you. Irradiated vapor and hot fragments cross your forearms; skin tightens and shines. Everything you touch finds the raw parts.

outcomes.success: You scratch a warning ring past the crater and walk before possession becomes a reason. The pulse shrinks behind you with every mile. Nothing opens beside your hands.
outcomes.failure: You mark the crater, reconsider the vanes, circle twice for a better look. Curiosity never touches, yet eats the daylight. Your next miles come more tired than deserved.

events.body:
A pilgrim sits against a blade of glass with their legs straight out in front of them, the way people sit when standing up has stopped being a plan. The robe has come apart at the shoulder and what shows underneath shines wet. Those burns are days old. They walked a long way carrying them.

One hand keeps a sealed purifier ampoule pressed to their chest. The other turns a metal prayer disk over and over: an eastern sun stamped on the face, a name scratched into the back that is not their own.

They say the name aloud twice, slowly, so that you will have it in your mouth and not only in your pocket. Carry it east. Somebody at the Citadel will know the rest of it, they say, and out here nothing proves it either way.

Between sentences the breathing goes shallow and quick. Real medicine would buy them time. The disk would only cost you the carrying.

outcomes.success:
You say the name back the way they said it, twice, and you do not pretend to know whose it was. That is the whole test. They press the disk into your palm and fold your fingers over it, then push the sealed ampoule after it, because an injector is no use to a chest that has stopped taking air properly.

What is left of their kit goes with it: wire, a split blade tang, buckles cut off a pack that died before its owner did.

They turn to face east while they can still choose which way to face. The disk weighs nothing until the breathing stops.
outcomes.failure:
The promise comes out of you too quickly and too smoothly, and they have heard smooth before, from pilgrims who took things east and kept walking. The hand around the ampoule does not open. They set it on the glass, weight a stone onto it, and lean until it cracks and drains into the fused ground.

The disk stays in the other fist. They die holding it. You walk east carrying a name nobody will ever ask you for, and you keep starting to say it out loud and stopping.

outcomes.outcome:
You cut the robe away where it has stuck, wash what is under it, and spend the sutures on the shoulder because the shoulder is what will kill them first. The kit goes into a stranger and does not come back.

They rinse your forearms and the back of your neck with the last of their bottle before they let you stand, because that is what the dust does if it is left to sit. They draw a line in the grit: the ridge road north of the hot ground, three markers, a dry cistern at the second.

They keep the ampoule. You leave steadier than you arrived.

events.body: Hundreds of thin antennas rise straight out of the fused plain, all holding the same low note. Their shadows point in conflicting directions, and small arcs cross between neighboring tips whenever the wind leans one toward another. At the field's center the tones change in a pattern too regular to be weather, coordinates folded inside a warning. Reading them would cost hours and turn all this noise into a bearing you could walk by. The quiet rows along the edge carry weaker current and offer a crossing that teaches you nothing.

outcomes.success: You separate the repeating group from the chorus by timing it against your own pulse, and once separated it will not hide again: the same bearing, over and over, folded inside a warning nobody stayed behind to hear. You mark it on your own map. For the first time in days you walk east without spending half your attention on the horizon.
outcomes.failure: Three frequencies line up inside your skull and refuse to come apart again. You leave the field on a bearing that keeps turning under you, stopping twice to be sick, and the ground will not hold level for the rest of the afternoon. The hours are gone and the pattern kept them.

outcomes.success: You move only when the quiet rows separate and stop whenever the humming climbs. No arc reaches you. The field closes behind with all antennas still singing, its hidden destination neither learned nor needed.
outcomes.failure: A bent mast enters the neighboring field as you pass. Current crosses your path in a white sheet, throwing you onto radioactive glass. You rise injured and contaminated before the charged rows can align again.

events.body: A cargo crawler lies fused belly-down across the plain, tracks sunk into black glass as if the ground swallowed it while hot. Its armored hold remains sealed beneath buckled plates. The driver’s hatch hangs open above a ladder glazed sharp by the flash. Cutting cargo access risks moving metal that still carries impossible strain. Climbing into the cabin offers a smaller prize and edges capable of opening skin with almost no pressure.

outcomes.success: You release the stressed plates in sequence and let each settle before entering. Riot padding, rifle cartridges, and a clean rifle optic wait inside a hold distorted around them. The crawler keeps its larger secrets beneath glass you cannot cut.
outcomes.failure: A plate folds along a heat-weakened seam and pins you flat to the chassis. You lever it off before your breath runs out, but the knee took the fold, and it fills the trouser leg while you sit on the glass looking at it. The hold stays shut above you, still holding its strain.

outcomes.success: You cover the hatch edges and lower yourself through the driver’s harness. Water sits beneath the seat beside a signal compass still tracking east. Its needle steadies the moment it enters open air.
outcomes.failure: A nearly invisible edge slices your forearm as you shift through the hatch. Blood makes every remaining handhold uncertain. You retreat and bind the wound before exploring farther, leaving the cabin and its unknown contents intact.

outcomes.victory: The colossus falls across the crawler's shadow with pilgrim offerings scattered through its armor. You gather resin sticks and rifle cartridges from its tribute hoard. Your stride stays hungry for the next fight.

events.body: Clear water bubbles steaming through cracked glass, ringed in white, green, warning yellow. No animal tracks near it. An open test-strip tin holds two strips. Its warmth could loosen your muscles — or its quiet radiation could bill you.

outcomes.success: Both strips settle on the same clean reading. The water runs metallic but safe, filling your bottles while heat eases fatigue. Steam covers the work.
outcomes.failure: The first reading lies: the spring’s pulse falls between color changes. Your meter tells truth after the bottles fill. You pour them out; the dose stays.

outcomes.success: You sit outside the mineral rings and let rising warmth into cramped legs and shoulders. Rest comes without a swallowed drop. You stand ready as the meter shifts.
outcomes.failure: Relief makes the pool feel safer every minute. You stay through one invisible pulse too many. Warmth leaves the muscles; a smaller radiation bill comes along.

events.body: Fused building shells multiply your reflection into a crowd that walks half a step out of time. Streets appear straight until mirrored walls return them from impossible angles. The broken sun remains visible in fragments above the roofline, offering direction if you can distinguish sky from reflection. Shadowed passages promise cooler travel, though their shelves of glass have cracked under decades of tension and sometimes settle without warning.

outcomes.success: You follow only the sun whose position changes when clouds move. False streets peel away from the route one by one. Your reflections remain trapped in side corridors while the real road opens east.
outcomes.failure: A mirrored sunrise draws you through the same intersection three times before its unmoving cloud exposes the lie. Lost hours consume strength and food. The reflected crowd seems better fed when you finally abandon it.

outcomes.success: You keep to the overhangs where the glass is still cool enough to put a hand on. The route bends constantly and never doubles back, which costs you a slow hour and none of the burning the bright avenues would have charged for the same distance.
outcomes.failure: A suspended shelf gives way above the darkest passage. Falling glass opens a line across your shoulder before you escape the collapse. You bind the bleeding beneath sunlight the safer route had asked you to avoid.

outcomes.victory: The mauler comes through the fused shells with its seams glowing. You work the plate gaps and drop it across its own slag. Its furnace plates fit your harness after cutting, and frame scrap fills your pack. Your hands stay hot and certain into the glass ahead.

events.body: Three sets of breathing keep pace beyond the reach of your lamp. They stop when you stop and start again one step after you move, which is discipline rather than accident. Turning now means picking the ground yourself instead of standing where they picked it. Killing the lamp costs you sight and costs them more, if the service alcoves you have been counting are where you think they are. The third road is two cartridges rolled into the open, and a pack that hears loose brass learns exactly what your pack is carrying.

outcomes.victory: You turn before the breathing reaches striking distance. Violence flashes across rails, pillars, and the narrow territory of your lamp. When the last hunter falls, pistol rounds, a smoke bomb, and a burst pipe-gun explain how patiently they planned for prey.

outcomes.success: Darkness takes both sides equally, but you counted the alcoves while light remained. You enter one without changing pace and let the hunters follow your fading footfalls. Their breathing passes close enough to warm the air.
outcomes.failure: Your shoulder finds a concrete pillar at full speed. The impact drops you hard and rings through the tunnel, giving pursuit a perfect bearing. You escape by moving concussed through darkness that now tilts beneath every step.

outcomes.success: The cartridges roll out of the light and stop against a boot you never see. Nobody thanks you. A voice low against the rail gives you three turnings and a warning about the fourth, and the breathing withdraws in order, unhurried, the way people leave a room they own. The line they sold you runs shorter than the one you had.
outcomes.failure: The brass lands and the breathing does not withdraw. It spreads. A knife comes out of the dark low and early, and you break their line with your forearm laid open and the price already gone from your pocket. What the offer bought them was proof that a full pack walks this stretch, and they will be listening for it.

events.body:
A subway train stands on dead rails with one carriage window lit warm yellow. Condensation clouds the glass from the inside, which means breath and bodies rather than a lamp somebody left burning.

Every other window on that carriage is covered. Route maps, blankets, a child's coat pinned flat, all of it arranged so the single bright square is the only thing anyone approaching can look at. From the roof hatch a wire runs off into the dark, thin and under tension, set where a hand reaching for the handle finds it before the handle.

Knocking hands your voice to whoever keeps the heat, and a voice travels a long way down a tunnel with nothing in it. The hatch asks nobody for anything and answers only to the wire. Shelter this far under usually survives by teaching strangers what surprise costs.

outcomes.success:
Your knock gets three taps back, spaced, a question in a code you do not hold. The lit carriage stays empty. The answer comes from the one behind it, where a connecting door slides a hand's width and a woman checks the tunnel at your back before she checks your face.

They feed you standing, from a pot on a stove built out of a fire extinguisher, and nobody offers a name. The heat gets into your legs before the food does. Before you go, a man opens your map on his knee and marks which junctions are theirs and which are not, pressing hard enough to score the paper.
outcomes.failure:
The window goes black between your second knock and your third. No footsteps, no bolt drawn, no voice. Warmth keeps leaking from under the carriage in a thin line along the ballast, so you know exactly how close they are standing while they wait you out.

You stay longer than pride allows and then walk the length of the train, and the covered windows go by one after another, and not one of them changes. Living people heard a stranger and chose the dark. It sits under your breastbone for hours afterward, and every quiet stretch of tunnel keeps handing it back.

outcomes.success:
You follow the wire to its anchor, take the tension off it, and lift the hatch by the hinge side. The carriage below is a stage set: benches squared away, a lamp burning steady behind glass, a blanket humped into the shape of somebody sleeping. Nothing in here has been breathed on for weeks.

Under the third bench sit two ration bars and a sealed bottle, placed where anyone robbing the decoy would find them first and go away satisfied. Further down the train, past two closed connecting doors, something metal is set down with great care, and then nothing moves at all.
outcomes.failure:
The wire is not wired to an alarm. It holds a counterweight you cannot see, and taking the tension off it lets the whole hatch plate swing on its arc.

The edge catches your shoulder and puts you off the roof onto the ballast, and your ankle folds under the landing. Nothing shouts. Nobody comes out. You get up in stages and go east past the lit square, which is still shining into a carriage arranged for an audience of one, and it does not so much as flicker while you limp out of its light.

events.body: Water shivers between rails before the roar arrives. A black surge rounds the bend with seats, dead lamps, branches. A ladder starts at shoulder height, rungs gone below — above the water, going nowhere. The platform lies downline, already covering.

outcomes.success: You jump, catch the first whole rung, and haul up as the surge fills the tunnel. The ladder bends and holds. You hang through it, then climb down thigh-deep.
outcomes.failure: Your wet hand slips as the flood arrives. Water slams you into tile, twisting a leg under debris. You climb out past the worst, injured and wrung by the current.

outcomes.success: You run the sleepers while the roar fills everything behind. The platform edge meets your hands one breath before water takes your feet. Its surge breaks harmless on concrete.
outcomes.failure: Hidden rubble turns your last stride into a fall. The surge rolls you through seats and black water onto the platform stairs. You rise battered, head unable to hold still.

events.body:
Shields cut from station signage close the platform stairs, EXIT and NORTHBOUND lashed to scaffold pipe with wire. Behind them somebody has aimed every working lamp outward, so you stand lit from four directions and the people asking the questions are shapes with voices.

They want to know why the Citadel should count for more than the food and the roof you have already used up getting this far east. They ask it the way a question gets asked when the answer has been wrong before, and recently.

Under the platform a pump coughs, catches, and coughs again. The sound goes through every pause in the conversation, and there is a woman at the end of the line who shuts her eyes each time it does. Two ways off these stairs: talk, or go down and put your hands into the thing everybody up here is listening to.

outcomes.success:
You give it to them plainly. The Citadel is a chance and not a promise, and you list what the road has already disproved before anyone up there can list it for you. Nobody interrupts, which is how you know it is landing.

The barrier comes apart at the hinge end, four hands lifting it clear. A man presses a medkit into your chest, the field kind with the seal unbroken, and tells you which of the two eastern tunnels takes water in spring. Behind him the pump is still coughing. You walk out with your reasons intact and somebody else's guarded hope pushing at your pace.
outcomes.failure:
Your reasons come out worn smooth, the road's own slogans in the road's own order, and you hear it happening while your mouth keeps going. The council lets you finish. That is the courtesy on offer.

Then the barrier opens and a woman with a tally board stands in the gap while another goes through your pack in front of everybody, taking what the platform charges for protection you have been standing inside since you arrived. They do not call it payment. You are in no position to call it theft. Whatever comes out of the pack goes into a crate already half full of other people's evenings.

outcomes.success:
The intake is choked with silt and one bootlace. You clear it by hand, cut a drive belt out of mismatched machinery, and set the tension by ear until the note stops climbing toward failure.

Water reaches the taps in a coughing rush and turns clear somewhere in the third minute. People come with cups and nobody watches you at all, which is the compliment. The council pays in purifier fluid, one sealed ampoule handed over with both hands, and walks you to the eastern maintenance gate personally so that the barrier never has to become an argument again.
outcomes.failure:
The housing takes your repair and holds pressure for four breaths. You are still listening for the note to steady when the belt goes, and the gears eat the new work along with every usable piece you were willing to feed them.

Water in the taps stays the color of the tunnel it came from. The council permits passage anyway, without a word, and it is the without-a-word that follows you east. Behind you somebody has already begun taking the housing apart again, doing it the slow way they were doing it before a stranger offered to be quicker.

outcomes.outcome:
You do not answer. The traveler at the end of the table does, in the flat voice of somebody who has said it before: a ravine on fused ground, a shelf of mirrored stone, a shadow walking with nothing over it, and a stranger who came down into the heat and took them out across open glass with the thing still moving behind them. Nobody interrupts.

The barrier comes apart at the hinge end. A man puts a field medkit into your hands, seal unbroken, and you walk off the stairs with the account somebody else was willing to give of you sitting in your chest like a second wind.

events.body: A route board points EAST down dripping-polished rails. West, a service door is welded along every seam, its conduit warm to the touch. Dust hides half the transfer diagram. A relay clicks each minute, and needles wander when it does.

outcomes.success: The bearing steadies past the relay. Behind the welded door, a service line runs straight at Citadel works. Knowing the route cuts distance and returns strength to your pace.
outcomes.failure: The needle chases interference through a collapsed loop, pointing back at the same sealed junction from behind. Hours of dark walking buy fatigue and proof instruments lie confidently.

outcomes.success: You strip the board to original paint, layer by layer, till transfer marks return: the dry bypass, the drowned sections. Your way out runs dry, direct, shorter than any bearing.
outcomes.failure: A works symbol mimics the Citadel mark in weak light. You follow it through a maintenance loop that eats time, strength, and food, arriving back at the board.

events.body: Stripped cable, ticket stubs, and other people's clothing fill the station office from floor to ceiling. Somebody has chalked STALKER on the door frame and cut three strokes beneath it, one for each time they came back and added another. Inside, something copies your footsteps at a delay too clean for echo, and when you shift your weight, cloth settles in imitation. Noise would bring it into the open before it has chosen its angle. One unchanged pace would give it nothing to correct toward.

outcomes.victory: Your first violent sound draws the Ash Stalker from its cable nest exactly where expected. The tunnel magnifies the struggle into thunder. After it falls, salvage and radiation tablets emerge from the possessions woven around its sleeping place, with a pale cloak and a sealed gland vial among them. Strips of stalk-hide lie cut for wrapping feet, and you take them.

outcomes.success: You maintain the same measured pace while copied footsteps multiply beside you. The mimic waits for a stumble that never comes. Its final imitation continues alone after you turn the corner.
outcomes.failure: Loose tile shifts under one heel and your rhythm breaks. The answering stumble comes from inside the office, followed by a rush. You escape its first strike wounded, fatigued, and shaken by footsteps that remain perfectly yours.

events.body: One vending machine glows at the end of a dead platform, its display requesting payment in a currency whose symbol no longer exists. Sealed food and water remain visible behind scratched plastic. The payment board can be reached through a narrow service slot carrying a steady electrical hum. Breaking the front offers direct access through safety glass designed to fragment inward, toward the hands of anyone impatient enough to test it.

outcomes.success: You bridge the purchase contacts without waking the alarm circuit. The machine dispenses food and water one item at a time, thanking an absent customer after each. Its light dies peacefully when the final bottle drops.
outcomes.failure: The anti-tamper cell releases its stored charge through your tool. Muscles lock and your forehead strikes the display before you fall clear. The machine remains lit, goods untouched, while concussion blurs its courteous payment instructions.

outcomes.success: You strike the panel along its weakened frame instead of the glass center. Plastic folds outward, yielding a ration and stimulant before the shelves jam. Enough remains visible to make restraint feel strangely expensive.
outcomes.failure: The safety pane behaves exactly as designed, showering inward across both hands. You withdraw bleeding before the opening is wide enough to use. Packaged food waits behind red-smeared glass you can no longer grip safely.

events.body: Pebbles drop from a bowed ceiling between two arches, a countdown with no last number. A steel post lies where someone dropped it — set under the weak span, it buys one careful walk. A cable duct runs low around the damage, dark at its far end.

outcomes.success: You seat the post under sound beam and cross as pressure groans through it in waves. The ceiling comes down behind your last step. Dust chases east; the weight stays.
outcomes.failure: The post punches through rotten concrete instead of spreading force. Slabs descend as you retreat, striking head and back. You crawl out concussed, injured, excavated.

outcomes.success: The duct widens past its turn and runs above the damage. You elbow-crawl it longer than the tunnel, dead cable on your back, and exit east with shaking knees.
outcomes.failure: The duct narrows at an old junction box and dies on poured concrete. Reversing the whole crawl eats strength and food. You return with less daylight and scraped patience.

outcomes.outcome: You set your shoulders under the fallen beam and heave until it sits straight on its mounts. The effort shakes old hurts loose and leaves you breathing easier.

events.body:
The signal ahead stands green, and every cable feeding it has been cut through. You can put a finger into the gap.

Green light lies flat across the standing water between the rails, and floating on it are curls of shed insulation, pale and light as bark, fresh enough that none of it has sunk yet. Along the powered run the lamps are dimming one after another in a traveling sequence, west to east, as though the load were walking. Twenty paces on, a cable tray sags downward under a weight the brackets were never cut to hold.

Under those lamps the maintenance marks are recent and deliberate, wiped clean by somebody's hand, and they aim east. A pencilled service note calls the thing in the tray a CABLE EATER. Old security systems also used green to walk authorized movement into ground they controlled. Cutting the feed would let you pass without answering either invitation, if the capacitors have not spent thirty years saving one last defense.

outcomes.success:
The markers repeat at every junction, each one cleared of dust within the last month, each turned to face the same way. You follow them through a tunnel shorter than any route you would have picked for yourself, and where the roof drips there are prints in the silt going both directions, the same tread twice.

Somebody maintains this line. Somebody expects traffic along it. Relief gets into your stride before the rest of it arrives: whoever cleans these markers knows the road is being walked, and by now has a fair idea of when.
outcomes.failure:
The green line ends beneath a restraint frame folded flat against the ceiling, dormant until your shin crosses its sensor. It comes down like a dropped shutter, strikes across your back, and holds at the end of its travel, quivering, while you get your boots under you again.

You pull clear. The frame retracts on its own, unhurried, and resets itself for the next one. The light above it stays green and stays exactly as helpful as it looked a minute ago. You go east flinching at lamps, and the flinch outlasts the bruise.

outcomes.success:
You ground the standing charge into the rail first, one hand on the tool and nothing else touching anything, and only then cut the feed. Green drains out of the water and out of the tunnel with it.

The dark that follows is honest dark. You walk it by hand and by count, and whatever those lamps were guiding, and whatever was drawing them along the run, has nothing whatsoever to say about you now. Behind you the line stays dead for as long as you can still hear it, which is most of an hour.
outcomes.failure:
The dead cable is not dead. The capacitor lets go through your cutters, your arms lock shut around the handles, and something throws you backward onto the ballast with your palms cooked and the smell of your own skin arriving a moment later.

You are upright inside a minute. The signal flickers, thinks about it, and comes back to green. You walk past it with both hands held away from your sides, and for the rest of the day grip is a decision you make rather than a thing your fingers do.

outcomes.victory:
The Cable Eater gives ground one segment at a time, then falls slack across the tray. Once its body stops bridging the cuts, the lamps quit walking and settle into a steady maintenance rhythm.

You pull usable copper and connectors from the gaps it kept alive. A wire-strung rifle hangs in the signal box, tuned rather than aimed, and you take it. The fixed lamps show the service marks in their intended order, enough to take the eastbound line without pretending a dead signal has made the Citadel safe. By the time you leave, the green has gone out for good.

events.body:
The blast door carries the first EAST CITADEL seal you have found intact. Stenciled, unscratched, the paint still holding its edges. Whatever else has failed down here, somebody kept this one.

Beside it a maintenance housing stands open on a cylinder seated in retaining teeth, and the plate above the teeth warns, in the flat language of procedure, about consumed tools and unauthorized extraction. Deep scoring inside the collar says the warning was written from experience.

Above that, a challenge display cycles six symbols and resets to black. It is a memory test with a flaw in it: the order shifts whenever relays click somewhere off to the east, so the sequence you are learning keeps being rewritten by traffic you cannot see. Take the cylinder and you carry hardware the door cannot reshuffle. Take the code and you risk nothing except being wrong.

outcomes.success:
You back the retaining teeth off in the order stamped beneath the housing, and the cylinder walks itself out of the collar into your palm, heavier than it looks and warm at the base.

Its shell comes apart into components worth carrying: contacts, a coil, two clean springs. The core stays whole. Somewhere past the door a mechanism turns over once and stops, the small definite sound a system makes when it writes something down. You have the hardware now. You are also, from this minute onward, a recorded fact at this seal.
outcomes.failure:
The housing accepts your improvised tool, rotates it a quarter turn past reach, and closes. The teeth do to the shaft precisely what the plate said they would, and what comes back out is not a tool any more, along with whatever you had wedged behind it to hold the angle.
